body.objective: Students will be able to describe clothing with colours.
body.iCan: I can describe clothing with colours.
successCriteria: I can name common clothing items in French

body.hook: You're at a shop in Montréal and want a blue hoodie in a medium. Can you ask for it? In French, colours change their spelling depending on what they describe, which sounds tricky but follows clear patterns. By the end of class, you'll describe what you and your classmates are wearing.

vocabulary.definition: To wear (Je porte… = I am wearing…).
Agreement: changing an adjective to match a noun's gender and number.

study.title: Qu'est-ce que tu portes ?
study.question: How do I describe clothing in French?
study.passage:
Colour agreement: in French, colours usually go after the noun and agree with it.
• Masculine singular: un chandail vert, un pantalon noir
• Feminine singular (add -e): une jupe verte, une veste noire
• Plural (add -s): des chaussures vertes, des pantalons noirs
• Colours already ending in -e don't add another: un t-shirt rouge, une jupe rouge
• Blanc becomes blanche in the feminine: une chemise blanche
• Orange and marron (brown) never change: des chaussures orange, une veste marron
Dialogue:
Chloé : Qu'est-ce que tu portes aujourd'hui ?
Noah : Je porte un chandail bleu, un pantalon noir et des chaussures blanches. Et toi ?
Chloé : Je porte une veste verte, un t-shirt rouge et une jupe grise.
Noah : J'aime ta veste !
Chloé : Merci ! J'aime porter des couleurs vives.
English support: Qu'est-ce que tu portes ? = What are you wearing? J'aime ta veste = I like your jacket. des couleurs vives = bright colours.
Activity: "Fashion show": each student describes what a classmate is wearing while the class guesses who it is.

body.hook: Before you buy a jacket in a boutique in Montréal, you'll want to know how much it costs and if it comes in your size. Today you'll learn numbers for prices and the questions shoppers ask.

study.title: Combien ça coûte ?
study.question: How do I ask and give prices in French?
study.passage:
Numbers for prices (written for this lesson): 20 vingt, 30 trente, 40 quarante, 50 cinquante, 60 soixante, 70 soixante-dix, 80 quatre-vingts, 90 quatre-vingt-dix, 100 cent. Examples: 75 soixante-quinze; 82 quatre-vingt-deux; 99 quatre-vingt-dix-neuf.
Prices: 24,99 $ = vingt-quatre dollars quatre-vingt-dix-neuf.
Questions: Combien coûte le chandail ? (singular) Combien coûtent les bottes ? (plural) Vous l'avez en bleu ? Vous l'avez en taille moyenne ? Quelle est votre pointure ?
Sizes: petit (S), moyen (M), grand (L).
Store flyer: un chandail 34,99 $; un jean 49,50 $; une tuque 15,00 $; des bottes 89,99 $; un manteau d'hiver 120,00 $; des mitaines 12,75 $.
Note: in Canadian French, un chandail is a sweater, une tuque is a toque and des mitaines are mittens.
Activity: partners ask and answer about flyer prices, then decide what they could buy with 100 $.
study.source: Original flyer and activity written for this lesson.

body.objective: Students will be able to role-play shopping.
successCriteria: I can play a customer or salesperson in a French shopping role-play
I can use polite expressions and ask for help

body.hook: Time to shop! In this role-play, you'll be either a customer looking for an outfit or a salesperson helping them, using everything you've learned about clothing, colours, sizes and prices.

vocabulary.term: Je le prends / Je la prends
payer par carte / en argent comptant

study.title: Au magasin
study.question: How do I shop for clothes in French?
study.passage:
Model dialogue (read in pairs):
Vendeuse : Bonjour ! Je peux vous aider ?
Client : Oui, je cherche un manteau d'hiver.
Vendeuse : Quelle taille ?
Client : Moyen, s'il vous plaît. Vous l'avez en vert ?
Vendeuse : Oui, voilà.
Client : Je peux l'essayer ?
Vendeuse : Bien sûr, la cabine d'essayage est là-bas.
(plus tard) Client : Ça me va ?
Vendeuse : Ça vous va très bien !
Client : Combien coûte-t-il ?
Vendeuse : Cent vingt dollars.
Client : Je le prends. Je peux payer par carte ?
Vendeuse : Oui, bien sûr. Merci et bonne journée !
Grammar: object pronouns le (masculine) and la (feminine) replace the item: le manteau → Je le prends. la robe → Je la prends.
Role-play: each customer gets a card (an occasion and a budget: e.g. "une fête, 80 $"); salespeople use the class flyer. Switch roles. Peers score with a checklist: greeting, item, size or colour, trying on, price, decision, payment, goodbye.
study.source: Original dialogue written for this lesson.
steps: Learn le and la as object pronouns
discussion: What does the customer look for?
Why "je le prends" for a coat?
Did you stay within your budget?
study.product: Perform a shopping role-play including all eight checklist steps and stay within your budget.
